messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the failing test does:
  - It constructs a CSVParser over the string "a\rb\rc" and sets the format’s line separator to “\r” (CR).
  - It then asserts that parser.getLineNumber() returns 1 immediately after construction.

- How getLineNumber is computed in the code:
  - CSVParser.getLineNumber() simply delegates to the lexer: return lexer.getLineNumber().
    - CSVParser.getLineNumber():
      - return lexer.getLineNumber();
    - Lexer.getLineNumber():
      - return in.getLineNumber();
    - ExtendedBufferedReader.getLineNumber():
      - return lineCounter;
  - Therefore, the reported line number is purely whatever ExtendedBufferedReader’s internal lineCounter says.

- Relevant behavior of ExtendedBufferedReader (from the issue report):
  - ExtendedBufferedReader increments its line counter when it sees ‘\n’ (LF) in its read() methods.
  - Its readLine() delegates to BufferedReader.readLine(), which recognizes CR, LF, and CRLF and discards the terminator.
  - Crucially, ExtendedBufferedReader does not increment the line counter when a line ends with ‘\r’ (CR) alone, because the counter update is tied only to ‘\n’ in read() and not to the outcome of readLine().

- Why this causes the failure for CR-separated input:
  - The format is explicitly set to use “\r” as the line separator, and the input contains CR as the only terminator (“a\rb\rc”).
  - Any reads performed by the parser/lexer during initialization or subsequent tokenization that encounter “\r” will not increment ExtendedBufferedReader’s lineCounter, because:
    - The read() path only increments on ‘\n’, not on ‘\r’.
    - The readLine() path consumes CR as a line terminator but ExtendedBufferedReader does not update the counter in tandem with readLine().
  - As a result, for CR-only line endings, lineCounter undercounts lines (commonly remaining at 0 when the test expects the starting line to be 1), and CSVParser.getLineNumber() returns the wrong value, making the assertion fail.

- Conclusion (root cause):
  - Inconsistent EOL handling in ExtendedBufferedReader: it counts LF but not CR. Since BufferedReader.readLine() treats CR, LF, and CRLF equally, ExtendedBufferedReader must likewise update lineCounter for CR (and CRLF) to keep the line number consistent across different line separators.
  - This mismatch makes getLineNumber incorrect when the format uses “\r” as the line separator, causing the test to fail.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
